t: A federation of the cities of Boeotia in central Greece, led by Thebes, with a common coinage stamped with the Boeotian shield.
Its fifth-century constitution of eleven districts and a representative council of 660 is one of the best documented in Greece.
Under Epaminondas and Pelopidas it broke Spartan power at Leuctra in 371 BCE and briefly led Greece.
dyk: The young Philip II of Macedon spent several years as a hostage at Thebes in the 360s BCE, at the height of Theban power, and probably learned from its generals.
ev: Boeotians fight on the Persian side and are defeated at the Battle of Plataea
Victory over Athens at Coronea leads to the refounding of the league
Pagondas defeats the Athenians at the Battle of Delium
The King’s Peace dissolves the league
Pelopidas and the exiles liberate Thebes and rebuild the league
Epaminondas defeats Sparta at the Battle of Leuctra
Roman envoys break up the league
